title: Closure retention and accidental memory leaks
hook: A closure keeps its outer lexical environment alive. If you store a closure in a global listener or timer, every variable it captured stays on the heap — even variables the closure never reads.

blocks.text: When a function closes over variables, V8 creates a **context** linking inner function to outer bindings. The **entire context** may be retained if any closed variable is needed — sometimes the whole scope object stays alive. **Accidental retention**: event handlers, `setInterval`, and module-level arrays holding callbacks capture large `request` or `DOM` graphs.

entries.plainDefinition: GC cannot collect reachable closure scope.
entries.example: Global array of handlers capturing req body.

blocks.text: Express middleware that registers `req.on("close", () => log(req))` retains entire request object until server restart if listener not removed. React useEffect missing cleanup retains stale props in closure.

blocks.title: Capture minimal data
blocks.body: Extract `const id = user.id` instead of closing over entire `user` object if handler is long-lived.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Reference stored
items.body: Timer, listener, or global holds inner function.

items.title: Context retained
items.body: All bindings in shared context may stay alive.

items.title: Fix
items.body: Remove listener, clear timer, or narrow captured values.

snippet.label: Failure — loop closure
snippet.explanation: var shares one binding; let creates per-iteration binding — retention and output differ.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Storing handlers without cleanup. Capturing entire request/config in long-lived callbacks. Using var in loop closures.

blocks.text: Chrome heap snapshot: find listener in retainers path to DOM or closure. Node: check `--inspect` allocation timeline during load test. Production: always return cleanup from subscribe helpers; weak references for metadata caches.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs
rows: Re-subscribe each render if not careful

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Says closures only capture used variables always — V8 context granularity varies. No cleanup strategy. Cannot read heap retainers.

interviewTakeaways: Closure = fn + lexical env; env kept while fn referenced.
Long-lived listeners/timers are classic leak sources.
Capture minimal fields; return disposer functions.
60s: Inner fn holds outer bindings. Global listener keeps huge object alive. Fix: off/clearInterval/narrow capture. let vs var in loop closures.
Follow-up: find leak in heap snapshot retainer path.
commonPitfalls: Weak: forget removeEventListener on SPA route change.
Weak: close over entire req in WebSocket handler.
Strong: narrow capture + cleanup + heap snapshot proof.
